main_body: Flat steel/metal wall face (blue-grey panels with an orange rail strip, rivets, a vent and two orange shelf bars), a wall tile drawn straight on
top_band: none (a wall face; only an orange rail strip at rows 5-6 and a light edge line at row 21 with no horizontal surface visible)
evidence: The kind is terrain (wall face), so it is a vertical face by nature. The scan shows an outline row, a dark blue band, an orange rail and then vertical panels with rivets and bars, all of them front-facing. Nothing is a horizontal surface seen from above. The wall tile is a flat front elevation, which is acceptable for wall-face terrain, but under the strict 3/4 contract no top band exists.

style.evidence: Only 14 distinct colours against 68 and 33 for the references, and a median of 9 colours per tile against 26 and 13. The flat-fill coverage is 30% while the references are at 0%. The large panel areas are single-tone blue-grey with no grain, speckle or per-unit shading. There are only about 4 lightness steps in the blue-grey ramp. The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is tonal rather than a black sticker line. The rivets and bars are tidy but the texture is much thinner than the timber and stone references.
